title: ML and AI for density functional theory: different priorities for Kohn-Sham and orbital-free DFT, for electronic and nuclear DFT
abstract: We overview similarities and, importantly, differences in computational bottlenecks and accuracy requirements that can be addressed with machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) techniques in electronic and nuclear DFT. From these follow different promising methodological and algorithmic choices depending on whether one machine learns the exchange correlation (XC) functional, the kinetic energy functional (KEF), the density or the basis functions. In particular, while the popular deep neural networks remain a potent choice in the context of KS DFT, we highlight their disadvantages when building KEFs and highlight conceptual advantages - yet to be fully realized - of symbolic regression for both electronic and nuclear DFT. We point out promising approaches that can be carried from the more extensively investigated ML-enhanced electronic DFT to nuclear DFT.
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive overview of applying Machine Learning and AI techniques to advance Density Functional Theory (DFT) for both electronic and nuclear structure calculations. It distinguishes between methodological needs when improving the exchange-correlation functional versus approximating kinetic energy functionals in orbital-free approaches. The work highlights that while deep learning is powerful, symbolic regression offers conceptually advantageous paths forward for achieving greater accuracy and efficiency.
main_problem: The paper addresses computational bottlenecks and accuracy limitations inherent in Density Functional Theory (DFT) when applied to both electronic and nuclear systems.
main_result: It outlines that different ML/AI techniques are suitable for improving DFT by targeting specific components like the exchange-correlation functional, kinetic energy functional, or density itself.
method: The authors survey various ML/AI approaches—including deep neural networks and symbolic regression—to enhance established quantum mechanical frameworks like Kohn-Sham (KS) and Orbital-Free DFT (OF-DFT).
model_or_system: The scope covers electronic systems (atoms, molecules) governed by the Schrödinger equation under the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, and nuclear systems involving nucleons interacting via the strong force. The core mathematical tool is the energy functional $E[ho(\mathbf{r})]$.
key_observables: Electronic observables include energies, band structures, and effective potentials; nuclear observables include binding energies, radii, and equation of state.
important_parameters: Computational scaling (e.g., cubic scaling in KS DFT), the unknown exact form of the exchange-correlation functional ($V_{XC}$), and system size are critical parameters.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that ML/AI can provide accurate, computationally cheaper approximations to intractable components of the DFT energy functional or Hamiltonian.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first reviewing the foundational physics and computational challenges in electronic vs. nuclear DFT, then systematically detailing how ML techniques can be applied to overcome specific bottlenecks (e.g., learning KEFs vs. XC functionals), concluding with a comparison of promising algorithmic choices.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter/nuclear theory, the deep dive into using symbolic regression and neural networks to approximate fundamental energy functionals is highly relevant for developing general-purpose, scalable numerical solvers applicable across quantum physics domains.
